text: It is the office of a prudent man to hinder all sort of anger and contention; in the exchange, that which springs from covetousness; in the fencing and wrestling schools, from emulation; in offices and state affairs, from ambition; and in a feast or entertainment, from pleasantness and joke.
author: Plutarch
locator: Symposiacs, Book I, What Manner of Man Should a Steward of a Feast Be?
